headline: MACKAY KICKS OFF 20,000M AT HISTORIC COMSTOCK — FIRST SYSTEMATIC DRILL ON OCCIDENTAL-BRUNSWICK LODE IN NEVADA (TSXV:MACK)
snippet: Mackay Gold & Silver Corp. (TSXV:MACK) started its inaugural 20,000-metre drill program on June 29, 2026 at the Comstock District property in Nevada — deploying shallow RC drilling over a 1,000 × 400-metre area at Occidental South targeting high-grade oxide gold-silver mineralisation, plus core drilling into the depth projection of the Occidental-Brunswick Lode, a multi-kilometre vein system running parallel to the famous Comstock Lode. With US$62 million in cash, Mackay is testing ground where the historic Sutro Dewatering Tunnel reportedly crossed a 30-metre-thick zone of mineralisation — the first large-scale, systematic exploration of this parallel structure in the district's history.

headline: SEVEN RIGS TURNING AT PLANALTO COPPER AS SECTION 232 CLOCK RUNS OUT — LARA'S BRAZIL VALIDATION REACHES 10,186M (TSXV:LRA)
source_name: Investing News Network / Lara Exploration Ltd. (TSXV:LRA)
snippet: Lara Exploration Ltd. (TSXV:LRA) reported June 29 that seven diamond drill rigs are operating concurrently at the Planalto Copper Project in Brazil's Pará state, with 29 holes totalling 10,186 metres complete toward the 14,000-metre validation target on the Homestead-Cupuzeiro trend. The program is confirming the geological model from the 2024 Mineral Resource Estimate and 2025 PEA at 100-metre grid spacing — with the Section 232 copper tariff report due to the White House on June 30, a validated-resource copper junior at scale is exactly the profile that M&A speculation tends to find attractive in the weeks after a tariff decision lands.

headline: SAGA ADDS SECOND RIG AT RADAR — 400M/DAY DOUBLES PACE TOWARD LABRADOR CRITICAL MINERALS MRE (TSXV:SAGA)
snippet: SAGA Metals Corp. (TSXV:SAGA) announced June 29 that a second diamond drill rig has arrived at the Radar Critical Minerals Project in Labrador, doubling daily advance capacity to approximately 400 metres, with one rig at Trapper North and one at Trapper South. With 13,149 metres completed across 64 holes — every hole showing oxide mineralisation — and a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate technical report targeted for later in 2026, Radar is entering its final systematic phase before resource definition.

headline: SAN LORENZO LINKS ARCO DE ORO TO SAN JUAN — EPITHERMAL SYSTEM CONFIRMED OVER 1.5KM OF STRIKE IN FOUR NEW HOLES (TSXV:SLG)
source_name: The Newswire / San Lorenzo Gold Corp. (TSXV:SLG)
snippet: San Lorenzo Gold Corp. (TSXV:SLG) announced June 29, 2026 that four drill holes at the San Juan Extension — the northwest extension of the Arco de Oro epithermal system at the Salvadora Property — confirm epithermal vein mineralisation reaching surface over an additional 0.5 kilometres of strike, extending the total confirmed system to over 1.5 kilometres. The system remains open to the northwest, and a new round of porphyry step-out drilling targeting the deeper system is planned to commence within approximately seven days.

headline: GERMANIUM SPLITS: WESTERN BUYERS PAY $6,150/KG AS AI FIBER BOOM DEEPENS CHINA CHOKEHOLD — 130% OVER DOMESTIC PRICE
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges documents a structural split in germanium pricing in June 2026: Western buyers sourcing in-warehouse material in the United States are paying US$6,150/kg — approximately 130% above the Chinese domestic benchmark of US$2,674/kg — as China's 2023 export licensing regime continues to choke supply to non-Chinese buyers. The driver is AI data center build-out: hyperscalers require up to 36 times more optical fiber than conventional servers, and with roughly 80% of global refined germanium produced in China, Meta's $6 billion commitment to Corning is the clearest signal yet that Western premium pricing for germanium shows every structural sign of persisting into 2027.

headline: CHINA BUYS 790+ TONNES SILVER AS SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT DEEPENS — SOLAR DEMAND BEATS RECORD MINE OUTPUT (GOLDSEEK SWOT)
snippet: US Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT report finds that China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in the first months of 2026 — driven primarily by solar panel manufacturing — as the global silver market runs its sixth consecutive structural supply deficit despite record mine production. China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material adds a sovereign accumulation layer to already-robust industrial demand, providing the kind of fundamental underpinning that macro-driven silver rallies typically lack. The SWOT analysis notes that silver's COT positioning reset — speculative net longs at 18-month lows — mirrors prior setup phases that preceded the sharpest silver recoveries of the current bull cycle.

headline: COT JUNE 26: GOLD SPEC LONGS AT 2024 LOWS — POSITIONING RESET AT LEVELS THAT HISTORICALLY PRECEDE SHARP REVERSALS
snippet: GoldSeek's Commitment of Traders analysis for the week ending June 26, 2026 finds gold speculative net longs compressed to levels last seen in mid-2024 — representing one of the most significant positioning resets of the current gold bull cycle. Historically, the sharpest gold recoveries of 2019, 2022, and early 2024 each began from precisely these positioning extremes; with silver speculative longs also at 18-month lows and U.S. dollar index speculative longs at their highest concentration since Q4 2025, the COT data is building a contrarian case for a near-term inflection that macro fundamentals alone cannot time.

headline: AFTER $4,000 BREAKS: NEXT SUPPORT AT $3,800 — TECHNICAL ROAD MAP FOR GOLD'S CORRECTION (CANADIAN MINING REPORT)
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's technical analysis of gold's correction identifies US$3,800–$3,600 as the next major support band after XAU/USD broke decisively below $4,000 for the first time since November 2025, extending the drawdown from January's $5,589 all-time high to approximately 28%. Deutsche Bank cut its year-end gold target to $4,800 from $6,000 on the same price action, while a death-cross pattern on the weekly chart points toward $3,400 in a worst-case scenario — the analysis provides a framework for position management and identifies the levels at which physical demand and institutional re-accumulation have historically stepped in.

headline: URANIUM Q2 RECAP: SPOT HOLDS $85–87 AS LONG-TERM CONTRACTS REACH $94 — REACTOR DEMAND OUTPACING NEW SUPPLY (INN)
snippet: Investing News Network's Q2 2026 uranium review finds spot prices consolidating in the US$84–87/lb range after surging past US$101/lb in January, while long-term contract prices have reached US$94/lb — their highest level since 2008 — as reactor restarts in Europe and Asia outpace new mine supply. With the Athabasca Basin's most advanced producing projects operating near capacity, the next tranche of supply depends on higher-cost ISR projects in the U.S. and Kazakhstan, a structural setup that supports the premium of long-term contracts over spot and, by extension, the development economics of junior Athabasca Basin explorers priced as though uranium were still at $75.
